title: openai-compat: harmonize tool_choice semantics and tool schema mapping with message formatting
author: Priya Malhotra
release_notes:
- Improve OpenAI-compatible tool_choice behavior: deterministic selection and explicit reason metadata
- Add schema mapping layer to translate OpenAI-style JSON Schema to Redwood tool arg shapes
- Normalize tool message formatting (system/assistant/tool role annotations) for streaming and structured output
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing tool registries; add comprehensive tests and compatibility harness
description:
Context: The OpenAI compatibility layer has supported basic function/tool calling but there have been inconsistencies across three dimensions: 1) tool_choice semantics (how/when the model indicates it wants to call a tool vs produce text), 2) mapping OpenAI JSON Schema-style tool argument payloads to Redwood's internal tool shapes, and 3) how tool messages are formatted/streamed to downstream consumers. Motivation: customers expect predictable, OpenAI-compatible behavior for migration and interoperability (notably for tool_choice + structured output). This PR consolidates the compatibility logic, tightens semantics, and adds tests.

Summary of changes (single-line checklist): - Implement deterministic tool_choice semantics: model-provided "tool_choice" object is honored when present; tie-break rules introduced when multiple choices exist. - Add schema-mapping layer in openai-compat adapter that validates and coerces incoming JSON Schema payloads to Redwood tool argument types (string/number/enum/array/object detection + required/optional handling). - Standardize tool message formatting: tool invocation messages now include explicit metadata fields ("__openai_compat":{"original_name":...,"schema_version":"v1"}) and consistent role annotations to improve streaming consumers' parsing. - Update streaming path so partial tool messages are buffered and flushed only once a full JSON payload (per schema) is seen or a terminal chunk is reached; this reduces malformed JSON in streaming consumers. - Add unit and integration tests validating compatibility against the openai-compat test harness and a small migration script to help operators opt in.

Why this approach: Instead of ad-hoc mapping in multiple places, a centralized adapter ensures a single source of truth for compatibility rules and simplifies future changes (schema upgrades, new tool_choice patterns). Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged unless a customer explicitly enables strict OpenAI compatibility mode via config flag (openai_compat: true).

Checklist before merge: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4211) - [x] Unit tests + integration tests added - [x] CI green (lint, unit, integration) - [x] Reviewer approvals (Dmitri, Sara) - [x] Compatibility-run against openai-compat harness

review_comments: Dmitri Ivanov: Left a few inline comments around edge cases where the model returns multiple tool_choice candidates: please add tie-break docs and a test.
Priya Malhotra (author): Added tie-break rules (timestamp + confidence score fallback) and added unit tests to cover duplicate candidates.

Sara Chen: Can we ensure the streaming buffer limit prevents unbounded memory usage for large tool payloads? Suggest adding a configurable max_buffer_bytes and a graceful fallback (emit error message).
Priya Malhotra (author): Added max_buffer_bytes (default 256KB) and a test to validate graceful fallback path.
